chapter: Clarinet and lessons with Jim Humphrey
title: The make of his clarinet and a hard-rubber clarinet that cracked
summary: Russell asks if it was a Buffet; Robinson recounts a fellow's rubber clarinet that broke at the joint after wiping it in the cold.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I remember if it could have been a buffet or Selmer or... No. Is it a French clarinet, do you think? It was made in Paris. Made in Paris. Yeah. Maybe Pencil Moller or something like that. Well, it might have been a buffet, but you don't know.

Yeah, it could be. Yeah, no, I never did notice the name on it. Yeah. Of course the name be on the barrel of it, you know. Yeah. I never did notice. I remember a fella had a clarinet. He bought it. And it was cold that night. We were re-oist. And when we got through there, we were putting them up, you know. Yeah. He pulled it like this, half into one of these coins. Oh, yeah. To wipe it out. Yeah. Yeah, it made out of this tough... Shammy skin they used sometimes. Yeah, like glass, you know, but it wasn't glass. He pulled it half into this, about that far from the metal joint. Yeah. And so he sent it back to the factory, I believe. It's a kind of a plastic stuff. Hard. Hard rubber. Yeah, yeah. The clarinet was made out of that. That's where it was. CG coin.
But the rag got stuck in the floor.
